newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: AUSTRALIA WON'T RECOGNISE CAMBODIAN GOVERNMENT YET
John Howard says Australia won't recognise the Cambodian Government, headed by the second Prime Minister Hun Sen, until it's recognised by the Cambodian people.
The PM says at this stage it's not necessary to evacuate Australian nationals from Cambodia, but aircraft in Malaysia are on standby.
He says Australia has been a great supporter of the Cambodian peace process and it's disappointing that the peace process has broken down.

"We're disappointed that the peace process to which Australia made a huge contribution including a force commanded by Colonel Sanderson which earned this country great distinction, has broken down" Mr Howard said.
"But in the end it is a matter for the Cambodian people to work out."
ONE NATION DEFENDS REMOVAL OF CAIRNS FROM MEETING
The One Nation party says it was entitled to remove former Whitlam government Deputy Prime Minister, Jim Cairns, from a meeting in Dandenong last night.
Mr Cairns was thrown out of the Dandenong Town Hall meeting, when he began handing out leaflets and refused to pay an entrance fee.
The National Director of Pauline Hanson's party, David Ettridge, says the decision was based on Mr Cairns' actions, and there were good reasons for his removal.
"One of those reasons was that he was distributing material that wasn't authorised and it's our forum for a public meeting not his," Mr Ettridge said.
Mr Ettridge said there was another reason he couldn't disclose saying Mr Cairns "was in no condition to be in that hall."
Ten people face criminal charges and one man is in hospital, after violent clashes, involving demonstrators outside the meeting.
CONSERVATIONISTS PICKET CABINET MEETING
Conservationists have picketed the Premier's Office in Townsville where Federal Cabinet is meeting.
The meeting is being used to highlight protests against the Prime Minister's Environmental record.
Chanting protesters urged Mr Howard and his cabinet colleagues to put the environment on the agenda, as they walked into the meeting.
The protest is primarily against the Port Hinchinbrook resort development between Townsville and Cairns.

Campaign Spokesman, David Haigh, says the Government's treatment of the issue reflects its dismissal of the environment "The way he treats the environment movement in this country is nothing short of a disgrace. In other words he won't speak with them," Mr Haigh said.
CABINET TO ADDRESS UNEMPLOYMENT
The Prime Minister has confirmed Cabinet will specifically address unemployment at a meeting in coming weeks.
Mr Howard says economic growth and greater flexibility in the labour market will result in lower umemployment.
He's told ABC radio in Townsville, prior to today's Cabinet meeting, that lower wages has resulted in a better employment record in the United States.
He says it's an argument that must be considered.
Mr Howard says he wants a proper debate about the causes of unemployment and for the community to understand the choices the nation has made in the context of that debate.
Meanwhile, Mr Howard says his government's honeymoon period is over, after polls published today show support for the Coalition has dropped to 43 per cent.
Mr Howard says there's consolation that the Government is still ahead of Labor.
"Any sort of temporary disenchantment people might feel with the Coalition is not being translated to an increased vote for Labor," he said.
COAL TRAIN CANCELLED AS PICKET CONTINUES
Railway authorities have cancelled a train which was due to go past pickets to load coal at the Hunter Valley Number one mine today.
The authorities are seeking help from the Industrial Commission in getting trains to the mine.
Striking mine workers have set up pickets in a dispute over an enterprise agreement.
The decision to cancel the train follows two failed attempts by mine management to load Freight Corp trains with coal, to take to the Port of Newcastle.
Yesterday, striking workers at the mine succeeded in blocking a train which had been chartered by the mine management to take 3,000 tonnes of coal from the mine to the Port of Newcastle.
Freight Corp representative Caitlin McKelvey says there's no point in sending trains when they aren't being loaded.
Meanwhile, ACTU President, Jenni George says unions affiliated with the mining industry will continue to take a stance against corporate giant, Rio Tinto.
Ms George told striking workers that they could expect support from the ACTU and mining industry unions.
She says the workers at Hunter Valley One are standing up for the rights of miners across Australia.

And Industrial Relations Minister Peter Reith yesterday warned unions considering secondary boycotts in support of the Miners' Union Hunter Valley strike, of laws against such action. The CFMEU has solidarity agreements with the Transport Workers' and Maritime Union, and it was thought these would be enacted if coal from the Hunter Valley Number One mine was shipped yesterday.
Mr Reith said workers away from the mine should be simply concerned about their own company's position, rather than trying to fight someone elses terms, conditions and negotiations.
US BLACK ACTIVIST READY TO FIGHT DEPORTATION ATTEMPT
American black activist, Lornzo Ervin, says he will fight to stay in Australia, if immigration authorities try to deport him.
The former Black Panther, who is currently touring the country, has been called to meet Immigration Department officials in Brisbane this afternoon.
Mr Ervin denies suggestions he's using false travel documents, and says he has nothing to hide.

He says he will co-operate with immigration authorities, and expects to be grilled on his reasons for being in Australia. Mr Ervin says if the Australian Government tries deport him, he will fight the action in the courts.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
